answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bundled, non-transferable work quota. Each operator holds timber: registration slots that refill only after thirty days of audited, distinct tasks. A new identity burns one slot, so fifty aliases cost fifty slots from a stock nobody can buy, and forging the audit trail costs more than the aliases can earn. Every operator also publishes a fable, a signed origin record, and the registry scores each new key by its hop distance from that origin. A key that fits no origin record is handled as a raven: throttled to one call per block until it earns a slot honestly.
